question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=5(3x-2)(x-k)$ is $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ The value of $k=$
question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{2},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{1}{2}.$ 

From the equation $y=5(3x-2)(x-k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=k.$  

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2}{3}+k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3k}{3})}{2} \\  & =\frac{2+3k}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2+3k}{6} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 2+3k & =3 \\ 3k & =1 \\ k & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
